A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Geodesic Calculus on Implicitly Defined Latent Manifolds by the same authors. All 24 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including equations, figures and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original geodesic interpolation and extrapolation experiments in Section 5, projection sensitivity results in Appendix A.3, and numerical comparisons in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical and visual outcomes in Section 5 and Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The denoising objective, projection-based representation, augmented-Lagrangian algorithm, metric choices and exponential-map procedure are retained. The corrected derivative sign in equation (8) leaves the zero constraint and computational procedure unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic examples, SCAPE shells, CMU motion capture, rotated-cow images and Pose-NDF pose experiments. The new Appendix D provides exposition without adding an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain linear and unconstrained interpolation, the Stochman parametric solver, Arvanitidis et al. (2018) RBF and Arvanitidis et al. (2022) sigmoid methods, and LAND. Their participation in Figures 13 and 15–18 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Experimental settings in Appendices A–C are unchanged, including the CMU 80/20 split, 10-dimensional SVAE, 30,000 cow images, and torus discretization and solver settings. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The projection sensitivity studies in Figures 10–11, metric and constraint comparisons, exponential-map robustness comparisons, and additional pose examples are retained unchanged. The added limitations and score discussion contain no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same reporting practice, without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental outcomes. The decoder-variance discussions concern unchanged model components.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Appendix C.1 retains torus path energies of 4.7889 for the proposed method and 4.7892 for Stochman, with optimization times of 1.89 and 2.48 seconds respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds the small-noise denoiser–score expansion and a Gaussian-distance special case relating the score to projection. Equation (8) corrects a multiplier-derivative sign. Appendix D largely specializes and explains existing geodesic mathematics; no full error-analysis proof is added.

C1.justification: The contribution statement now explicitly qualifies the geodesic interpretation as applying to regular, smooth data manifolds, while describing the general output as realistic interpolation and extrapolation. It also adds a code contribution; the abstract and central learned-projection claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly acknowledges untested scalability beyond latent dimension 84 and the absence of a combined mathematical error analysis. It extends the existing distance-evaluation caveat with a possible learned-distance workaround. Appendix A.3 adds a substantive interpretation connecting projection residuals to scores and diffusion models.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a link to the authors' LatentGeodesics code and states that it supports different metrics and implicit representations. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resource's contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kharitenko et al. (2026) and Song et al. (2021) for the score connection, and Birgin and Martínez (2014) and Kanzow et al. (2018) for optimization scalability. The broader positioning is retained; consolidation of duplicate Lobashev references is bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated Limitations section and an intuitive geometry Appendix D, expands the background and score explanations, and updates contribution wording and appendix cross-references. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All 18 figures retain their scientific content. Layout changes include placing Figures 3–4 together and Figures 13–14 together, with other figures and surrounding text repositioned as the document reflows.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and transparency through the qualified contribution statement, explicit scalability and error-analysis limitations, and the intuitive Appendix D. The code pointer also improves access documentation. These are useful but limited gains: the empirical evidence is unchanged and the acknowledged validation gaps remain unresolved.
